bull_bear.body:
- Multi-location manufacturing infrastructure at Ankleshwar and Surat (stated Strength in the MD&A SWOT)
- Strong production capabilities and high capacity utilisation - approximately 18 tons per month against approximately 22 tons per month installed capacity at both plants
- Export-oriented business model serving a niche and specialised market (stated Strength in the MD&A SWOT)
- 350 kVA ground-mounted solar renewable-energy infrastructure at Ankleshwar, supporting energy cost and sustainability positioning
- Kosher-certified Ankleshwar facility, which the Company states widens access to international customers and markets requiring recognised certification
- Experienced management and established industry knowledge (stated Strength in the MD&A SWOT)
- Wholly-owned subsidiary HSDL Innovative Private Limited providing additional business and operational synergies
- Established pharma marketing and distribution network across multiple states, diversifying the revenue base alongside freeze-drying
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price volatility and availability — MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' names fluctuations in raw material prices and availability first; the SWOT lists 'Exposure to fluctuations in raw material costs' as a weakness and 'Volatility in raw material prices' as a threat. Freeze-drying converts agricultural produce, so input cost moves directly into gross margin.
- Seasonality of agricultural produce — The MD&A cites seasonality of agricultural produce among its risks and the SWOT lists 'Dependence on seasonal availability of certain raw materials' as a weakness - a structural constraint on year-round plant loading and product mix.
- Export exposure to tariffs, duties, logistics costs and overseas trade policy — The Company states its export-oriented operations may be affected by changes in tariffs, duties, logistics costs and regulatory requirements in overseas markets, and lists 'Changes in international trade policies and tariffs' as a threat. Exports are a stated strategic focus (approximately Rs 1.01 crore of turnover in FY 2025-26), so trade-policy shifts hit the growth vector directly.
- Foreign exchange fluctuations — Named both in MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' and as a SWOT threat, and again in the cautionary statement; the Company sells into overseas markets and is building an export platform, so realisations are FX-sensitive.
- Capital intensity of freeze-drying manufacturing — The SWOT's first weakness is that 'Freeze-drying remains a capital-intensive manufacturing process'. With two plants and a newly added freeze-drying machine, fixed costs and depreciation are carried whether or not volumes fill the added capacity.
- Under-utilisation of newly added capacity — Both the Ankleshwar and Bhatpore, Surat facilities ran at approximately 18 tons per month against installed capacity of approximately 22 tons per month, and the SWOT flags 'Greater utilisation of the new Surat manufacturing capacity' as an opportunity still to be captured. Management's own outlook makes improved capacity utilisation a condition of growth, 'subject to prevailing market conditions'.
- Competition from domestic and international players — Listed as a threat in the SWOT and among risks in the MD&A; the Company describes freeze-drying as a niche, specialised market where customers can be won on technology, quality systems and scale.
- Weak domestic retail penetration against a brand-led pivot — The SWOT weakness is 'Relatively developing domestic retail penetration', yet the stated strategy is to move from manufacturing into consumer brands (FZYEZY, OXYNXT). The MD's own message concedes that building a consumer brand 'requires patience, investment and, above all, an understanding of the consumer' - execution risk on an unproven channel.
- Regulatory and certification requirements in international markets — Listed as a SWOT threat and repeated in the exports section; access to overseas customers depends on holding the right certifications (the Ankleshwar plant obtained Kosher certification during the year), and changing requirements can close markets.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Incorporated in 2007 in Gujarat, Hamps Bio runs a Pharma Marketing Division that markets and distributes pharmaceutical and nutraceutical products through an established marketing and distribution network across multiple states in India, and a Freeze-Drying Division that manufactures freeze-dried fruits, vegetables, herbs, flowers, powders, nutraceutical ingredients and ready-to-eat products for B2B, D2C, domestic and export customers in food, beverage, nutraceutical and confectionery applications. The Company describes itself as moving from a manufacturing-led business towards a brand-led organisation, building its own consumer brands Fzyezy and Oxynxt. HSDL Innovative Private Limited, which operates in the value-added food and freeze-dried products segment, became a wholly-owned subsidiary during FY 2025-26.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Freeze-Dried Ingredients:** freeze-dried fruits, freeze-dried vegetables, herbs, flowers, powders, nutraceutical ingredients, ready-to-eat products, Fzyezy (consumer brand), Oxynxt (consumer brand)
- **Pharma Marketing:** pharmaceutical formulations, healthcare / nutraceutical products across several therapeutic categories
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- HSDL Innovative Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly-owned subsidiary, 100% shareholding, acquired 25.03.2026 (reporting period for the subsidiary 25.03.2026 to 31.03.2026 per Form AOC-1). Operates in the value-added food and freeze-dried products segment; appears in the related-party note as a purchase and sales counterparty.
- V4U Healthcare Private Limited — related party: Described in the related-party note as an 'Associate Concern'; Herrik Shah and Shrenikkumar Shah are both directors of it. Form AOC-1 Part B separately states the Company has no associate companies or joint ventures, so this is a related party by KMP control rather than an accounting associate. Appears as a sales and rent-income counterparty.
- M/s Mahavir Medicine — related party: Enterprise over which KMP has control - Herrik Shah is the proprietor. Appears as a sales counterparty in the related-party note.
- M/s Adinath Medicine — related party: Enterprise over which KMP has control - Herrik Shah as Karta of the HUF. Appears as a sales counterparty in the related-party note.
- Herrik Shah HUF — related party: Listed under relatives of Key Managerial Personnel in the related-party note.
- Mountbaton Shah HUF — related party: Listed under relatives of Key Managerial Personnel in the related-party note.

outlook.body:
- Move beyond being only a manufacturer and evolve from a manufacturing-led business into a brand-led organisation, developing and scaling its own consumer retail brands with particular focus on FZYEZY and OXYNXT
- Increase utilisation of the existing manufacturing infrastructure at Ankleshwar and Bhatpore, Surat
- Expand the domestic and international customer base, increase export opportunities and develop new overseas markets
- Develop customised and value-added freeze-dried products, including customised ingredient development and contract-manufacturing opportunities
- Improve operational efficiencies and production yields
- Leverage the capabilities and infrastructure of wholly-owned subsidiary HSDL Innovative Private Limited to create Group operational synergies, additional revenue contribution and product development
- Strengthen quality and certification systems to meet international customer requirements
- Increase brand presence in retail, distribution, the franchise market and e-commerce platforms
- Continue focus on sustainable manufacturing and renewable energy
- Maintain disciplined capital allocation, prudent cost management, efficient working-capital utilisation and stronger financial controls as the business expands (CFO message)
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY 2025-26 was described by management as a year of capacity expansion and infrastructure development. The Bhatpore, Surat manufacturing facility was expanded and developed and has now progressed into full-fledged production operations, significantly strengthening the Company's overall manufacturing capacity and adding infrastructure to serve a growing customer base. Both plants - Ankleshwar and Bhatpore, Surat - ran at production of approximately 18 tons per month against installed capacity of approximately 22 tons per month during the year. A new freeze-drying machine with a daily processing capacity of approximately 450 kg was added at the Surat facility; management expects this equipment to increase production capability and contribute incremental revenue in the ensuing financial year. The Company also commissioned and operationalised a 350 kVA ground-mounted solar power plant at the Ankleshwar facility as part of its renewable-energy and carbon-footprint reduction commitment, and the Ankleshwar facility obtained Kosher certification during the year. On the inorganic side, HSDL Innovative Private Limited became a wholly-owned subsidiary on 25 March 2026 (100% equity acquired), extending the Group's presence in the freeze-dried and value-added food segment and providing, in management's words, additional revenue contribution and operational synergies. Going forward, the stated focus is on raising utilisation of the existing infrastructure, greater utilisation of the new Surat capacity, developing customised and value-added products and improving production yields. No rupee capex quantum is disclosed anywhere in the routed narrative.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The global food and nutraceutical industry continues to witness increasing demand for products offering convenience, extended shelf life, nutritional value and natural characteristics; freeze-dried products serve food ingredients, nutraceuticals, ready-to-eat and other value-added food categories
- Increasing preference for clean-label, natural and convenient food products creates opportunity for manufacturers possessing appropriate technology, quality systems and scalable production capabilities
- Management believes freeze-drying growth will come through increased B2B ingredient supply, development of customised products, expansion of finished products and greater penetration into international markets
- The full-fledged operations of the Bhatpore, Surat facility, higher utilisation of existing infrastructure, addition of new freeze-drying capacity and integration of HSDL Innovative Private Limited together give the Company a stronger platform for future growth
- The new freeze-drying machine of approximately 450 kg per day at the Surat facility is expected to provide additional production capability and support incremental revenue generation in the ensuing financial year
- Expanded manufacturing infrastructure, additional freeze-drying capacity and certifications such as Kosher are expected to support access to a broader range of international customers and markets
- The Company expects continued improvement in capacity utilisation, export opportunities, revenue generation and overall operational efficiency during the ensuing financial year, subject to prevailing market conditions
- Headwind flagged: global trade conditions, tariffs, foreign exchange movements and overseas regulatory requirements may influence the export business from time to time
- Rising international demand for freeze-dried and health-oriented food products, and rising demand for nutraceutical and wellness products, are the stated Opportunities in the MD&A SWOT
